prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 1997 manifesto (policy-focused, non-ideological)

Education and skills
- Invest £2bn per year in education via a 1p rise in the basic income tax rate.
- Universal high-quality early years education for 3–4 year-olds.
- Double school spending on books/equipment in year one; cut primary class sizes to max 30 within five years; £500m over five years for repairs.
- General Teaching Council; focused Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; stronger inspections; literacy drive.
- End Assisted Places Scheme; integrate grant-maintained schools/CTCs into a common local framework; oppose selection but let local communities decide.
- Individual Learning Accounts; income-linked loan repayments; oppose tuition top-up fees; credit-based system for post-14; all schools online.
- 2% remissible training levy on company payrolls (small firms exempt); aim for 16–19s to receive at least two days/week learning or training.

Economy, enterprise, consumers
- Central bank independence with an anti-inflation mandate; adhere to a “golden rule” on borrowing; clarify capital vs current spending; expand PPPs.
- Shift tax from jobs/consumption to pollution/resource depletion; promote saving via broadened save-as-you-earn and portable pensions.
- Improve SME finance, late-payment interest rights, cut “gold-plating” of EU rules; long-term goal to replace the Uniform Business Rate.
- Regional Development Agencies; reorient R&D from military to civil; promote employee participation, profit-sharing, and stronger shareholder oversight.
- Stronger competition authority; ombudsmen; improved product/eco labelling (incl. GM ingredients); single utilities regulator; tighter financial services oversight.

Environment, energy, transport
- Targets including a 30% CO2 cut from 1990 levels within 15 years; annual national report on progress; create a dedicated environment/energy department.
- National Home Insulation programme targeting fuel poverty; phased carbon tax offset by cuts to VAT/employers’ NICs; lower VAT on conservation materials.
- Promote renewables and CHP; no new nuclear subsidies; focus on decommissioning and waste management.
- Invest in public transport; enable urban road pricing; keep London Underground public with access to private finance.
- Rail: treble freight and double passengers by 2010; enforceable targets; potential reacquisition of Railtrack control if persistent failure.
- Cut annual car tax to £10 for ≤1600cc, funded by ~4p/litre fuel duty rise; reform company car tax.
- Stronger water quality rules, leakage targets, fairer charging, excess profits sharing; wildlife protections; producer responsibility, deposit-refund schemes.
- Animal welfare: testing bans for cosmetics/weapons/tobacco; stricter transport/rearing standards; national dog registration; tighter endangered species protections.

Health and care
- Immediate 6‑month halt to finance-driven closures with independent audit.
- At least £540m extra per year; £200m/year for frontline staffing (e.g., 10,000 nurses or 5,000 doctors); national pay structure; reduce bureaucracy.
- End two‑tier GP system; National Inspectorate for Health & Social Care; cut waits to max six months in three years.
- Restore free eye and dental checks; freeze prescription charges funded by +5p per cigarette pack.
- Improve NHS dentistry access; stronger patient rights; more local accountability; prevention focus; independent Food Commission.
- Community care: extend choice, create Carer’s Benefit, national standards/charging guidance.

Crime, housing, communities
- 3,000 more police; cut paperwork; restorative justice for youth; early intervention; CPS overhaul; crime-prevention partnerships; victims’ support; Royal Commission on drugs.
- Housing: build more via public/private/housing association partnerships; release council capital receipts; allow local borrowing within controls.
- New Mortgage Benefit for first-time buyers (replacing MIRAS for new borrowers); end rough sleeping by 2000 via rent deposit schemes and hostels; stronger tenant rights; bring empty homes into use.

Governance and constitutional reform
- Bill of Rights (ECHR in UK law); Human Rights Commission; Ministry for Justice; Freedom of Information Act; reduce quangos; use referendums on major constitutional issues.
- Commons reform; reduce MPs by ~200; predominantly elected second chamber; proportional representation for all elections; fixed 4‑year terms; party funding transparency/limits.
- Devolution: legislatures for Scotland and Wales with tax-varying powers; elected English regional assemblies where demanded; London authority.
- Strengthen local government finance and powers; long-term shift to Local Income Tax and locally set business rates.
- Northern Ireland: power-sharing, proportional voting, civil liberties safeguards, reformed security procedures, economic cooperation; participation in talks contingent on renouncing violence.

Welfare, work, equality
- Benefit Transfer Programme for long-term unemployed; raise personal allowance by £200 (nearly 500,000 lifted out of tax), funded by a new 50% rate over £100k; replace Income Support/Family Credit with a simpler Low Income Benefit improving work incentives.
- National childcare strategy; voluntary Citizens Service; regionally variable minimum wage; tackle fraud and tax evasion.
- Older people: earnings-linked top‑up for low-income pensioners; flexible retirement 60–70; anti‑age discrimination; replace SERPS with funded personal/occupational pensions; portability; abolish water standing charges.
- Young people: restore benefits for 16–17s; expand youth services; citizenship/parenting classes.
- Families: replace Child Support Agency with unified family courts; parental leave and flexible parental benefit; adoption/fostering based on suitability.
- Women: pro‑rata rights for part‑timers; enforce equal pay; pension reforms; better NHS access; stronger protections against domestic/sexual violence; targets for women on public bodies.
- Disabled people: comprehensive civil rights; Partial Capacity Benefit; access standards; stronger SEN support.
- Ethnic minorities: merged equalities commission; enforce CRE code; fair housing allocation; non‑discriminatory immigration; restore asylum benefits with faster decisions; address discriminatory policing.
- LGBT: equal age of consent; outlaw discrimination (incl. armed forces); repeal restrictive local government clause; tackle homophobic crime.

Europe, foreign policy, defence, trade
- Constructive EU engagement; referendums on major changes; more majority voting with key vetoes retained; PR for MEPs by 1999.
- Join a single currency if Maastricht criteria are met and approved by referendum.
- Strengthen EU foreign/security cooperation; police/customs cooperation; reform CAP to direct payments; replace CFP with regional stock management; end quota‑hopping.
- Maintain defence capability at current levels; retain Trident with reduced warheads; support CTBT and NATO enlargement.
- Strengthen UN peacekeeping (on‑call forces, training, command); support an International Criminal Court.
- Lead on global environmental agreements and institutions.
- Increase aid on a timetable toward 0.7% GNP within 10 years; debt relief; tie aid to human rights.
- Tight arms export controls; UN arms register; total landmine ban.
- Freer trade with labour and environmental standards; global competition policy.

Tax transparency
- Annual “Tax Contract” on how money is raised/spent; costed pledges; waste reduction before tax rises; fairer burden sharing.
